newsitem.title: NORWAY: Hydro drags down Oslo index, Aker inflates trade.
newsitem.headline: Hydro drags down Oslo index, Aker inflates trade.

text.p: Industrial heavyweight Norsk Hydro fell in late afternoon trade to burden the Oslo Total index, breaking an 11-session streak of record closes.
The Total index finished 0.02 percent off at 925.12 points in very healthy trade worth 1.5 billion crowns, including more than 600 million crowns in engineering and offshore group Aker.

The index climbed to an intra-day trading high of 932.20 points before Hydro, which has a 20-percent weighting on the index, started trading in negative territory. Hydro finished 0.6 percent lower at 319 crowns possibly because of profit-taking and lower aluminium prices, one dealer said.
Another said: "The market was very strong. Then someone pulled the plug. People started selling. Maybe it was time for it."
Aker's A class share finished marginally lower at 143.50 crowns after state pension fund Folketrygdfondet said it had sold four million A shares in the group.
The stock market has been strengthened by falling interest rates and good liquidity in the past two weeks as well by Wall Street's rally.
